text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Solaris Finance (tenant: solaris-prod) — spike in 5xx errors on dedicated pool eu-west-1/ded-solaris-phi. P50 latency x2, error rate +18% over 5m. Paging oncall.

oncall-lee: I'm on. Pulling logs now, adding incident label solaris/5xx. Is this isolated to the dedicated pool or touching their VPC?

sre-maya: Confirmed: dedicated pool ded-solaris-phi. Errors look like OOMs and kv-cache misses after ~512 tokens. Sample error: "runtime: kv-cache allocation failed" followed by 502 gateway.

oncall-lee: Thanks. Quick customer impact check: @acct-julie are live prod users impacted or only background jobs? We should avoid semantic-changing swaps if prod is live.

acct-julie: Live prod is seeing timeouts for some users (payments flow). We need to preserve response semantics where possible; any replacement must be conservative.

eng-ryan: Proposal: divert a fraction of NEW sessions to a conservative, quantized safe variant (redwood-small-safe-v1) to reduce memory pressure, and pin existing active sessions to the last known-good model (redwood-large-stable-2026-02-14) so in-flight contexts are unchanged. This avoids sudden behavior changes mid-session.

platform-rob: We can add a routing divert rule scoped to tenant solaris-prod for new sessions only. Start at 30% new-session diversion, monitor metrics, then increment. If quality holds, scale to 60-80%. I'll apply if oncall approves.

oncall-lee: Approved. Apply 30% divert and pin existing sessions to stable model. Share exact API call.

platform-rob: Applying rule now. Command:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/routing-rules \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"tenant":"solaris-prod","scope":"new_sessions","target_model":"redwood-small-safe-v1","percent":30,"condition":"!session.pinned"}'
```

eng-ryan: Pin active sessions with this snippet (affects only existing session objects):
```
POST /v1/tenants/solaris-prod/sessions/pin 
  {"session_ids": ["list-of-active-session-ids"], "model": "redwood-large-stable-2026-02-14"}
```
(I'll run a quick script to enumerate and pin high-traffic sessions.)

oncall-lee: Running pin + diversion now. Will report back with traffic/5xx numbers in 2m.

platform-rob: Routing rule accepted and deployed -> rule_id=rr-8342.

ops-bot: metric-update solaris-prod 1m: 5xx_rate down 62% on diverted hosts; p50 latency down 28%; kv-cache errors down 70%.

acct-julie: Early feedback from support: diverted responses are slightly shorter but within tolerance for payments flow. No functional breakages reported.

sre-maya: Memory profiles show peak working set reduced ~40% on nodes handling safe variant. OOMs have ceased on those nodes.

oncall-lee: Nice. We'll keep diversion at 30% for 15 minutes, then consider increasing to 60% if trends hold. Also scheduling a warm-standby reserved slot to move solaris entirely off the noisy shared hardware if needed (low-risk, takes ~10m to drain).

platform-rob: Standby reserved capacity can be spun up; require approval from infra-quota team — I've opened infra ticket #INC-11902. If granted, we can migrate with no client-visible cutover (drain then swap).

eng-ryan: One more precaution: lock model rollout for solaris-prod in the control plane so automated experiments / A/B doesn't flip variants during the incident. Command:
```
PATCH /v1/tenants/solaris-prod/config 
{"auto_experiments": false, "model_rollout_lock": "manual"}
```

oncall-lee: Done. Rollout lock applied.

ops-bot: Alert note: incident acknowledged by oncall-lee; automated escalation paused.

platform-rob: Metrics at +8m post-change: 5xx down 75% globally for solaris-prod, latency stabilizing. I'll hold at 30% until oncall says to scale.

oncall-lee: Agreed. If numbers remain steady at +15m, increase diversion to 60% and revisit customer execs. If quality regressions appear, revert rule (platform-rob has rollback slug).

acct-julie: Please keep me posted before any change >30% — I will notify account team + PM. Also preparing a short customer-facing note in case we need to advise a temporary performance degradation.

sre-maya: Adding follow-up items: (1) investigate root cause for kv-cache allocation spike (likely input distribution), (2) add a protective quota for large prompt sizes for this tenant, (3) add a memory guardrail to avoid host OOMs.

oncall-lee: Thanks team. I'll keep monitoring and will update channel at +15m or earlier if anything changes. :thumbsup: 

incident-bot: Incident log updated: strategy=diversion+session-pin+rollout-lock; status=monitoring. Runbook ref: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/solar-incident-2026-03 (private).
